Objectives: Resolve high-impact assumptions and source conflicts that block build execution, confirm policy decisions, and finalize nonfunctional and governance baselines before implementation accelerates.
Success Criteria: Priority identity, residency, and collaboration-channel decisions are confirmed; integration and verification approach is ratified; unresolved items are explicitly accepted as assumptions with owners.
Dependencies: Inputs from discovery and requirements baseline
Risks: Decision latency on policy-heavy questions can delay start of build phases.

Objectives: Establish the patient digital front door with registration, authentication, onboarding workflow, and profile gating while preparing security and migration controls that underpin later lifecycle work.
Success Criteria: Patients can register and complete onboarding; baseline controls for regional security and migration planning are implemented and testable.
Risks: Identity-policy drift or unresolved onboarding edge cases can cascade into downstream lifecycle and migration scope.

Objectives: Implement subsidy application orchestration, eligibility checks, and standardized status lifecycle while advancing migration/security execution for controlled cutover readiness.
Success Criteria: Eligibility flow handles core pathways with auditable decisions; lifecycle states are consistent across regions; migration/security controls are integrated into lifecycle processing.
Risks: External checker latency and unresolved verification evidence model can reduce automation quality and increase manual triage.

Objectives: Deliver practitioner assignment and reassignment logic, assessor work management, escalation visibility, and collaboration pathways that complete the operational model.
Success Criteria: Assignment and escalation flows run against agreed rules; assessor work queues and collaboration channels are operational with traceable routing.
Risks: Unconfirmed geospatial-matching approach and channel architecture can force late design changes.

Objectives: Execute migration cutover controls, stabilize production behavior, and close readiness gaps with focused defect hardening and adoption support.
Success Criteria: Cutover executes with reconciled data and controlled access; high-priority defects are resolved; operational teams confirm readiness for steady state.
Risks: Late discovery of migration data quality issues or unresolved policy items can extend stabilization.
